newsitem.title: USA: Prospects for U.S. banking reform unclear - Leach.
newsitem.headline: Prospects for U.S. banking reform unclear - Leach.

text.p: Prospects for enactment of broad banking reform are unclear when compared with last year, House Banking Committee Chairman James Leach said Tuesday.

"I see more prospect than two years ago, but it is clearly unclear whether the Comptroller's action will be of a precipitating or retarding nature for comprehensive reform," he told reporters after speaking at an investors conference.
The Comptroller of the Currency recently approved a regulation that would allow, on a case-by-case basis, a bank to conduct activities in a subsidiary not allowed the bank itself.
Leach, a Republican from Iowa, said the House was unlikely to repeal the Comptroller's ruling.
He planned to introduce legislation at the start of the new Congress that would dismantle the Depression-era Glass-Steagall law by allowing banks to affiliate with securities and insurance firms.
Leach was asked whether there was much appetite in Congress for addressing the budget deficit through some tinkering with the consumer price index.

"I don't see a great appetite for any confrontational discourse on the subject. If the Administration were to put its weight behind an approach I think the Congress might be prepared to look at it seriously," he said.
